Practice note · editorial draft

How I use AI in research

AI can help prepare research work. Sources, code and findings then need to be checked.

I find AI useful for specific tasks: refining a question, organising a literature review or preparing a coding plan. It can also help clarify an explanation. The response depends on the context and documents it receives.

When AI suggests a source, I treat it as a lead. I need to find the original document, check its authors and date, and read the passage that supports the argument. A reference that sounds plausible may be false.

For analysis, the script has to be run and checked. The researcher remains responsible for units, missing observations, variable construction and model choice. A convincing explanation is not enough to validate a coefficient.

I therefore keep a record of decisions, code and limitations. AI can speed up preparation and communication. The researcher remains responsible for interpretation and validation.

About this note

An editorial draft to review before public release. It presents neither an empirical study nor a technical implementation.
